title: Trial of Chaos: Modifiers, Room Loops and Fate to the Trialmaster
summary: How the Trial of Chaos ten-room loop works in Path of Exile 2: choosing Tribulations, which modifiers brick which builds, the reward ladder, Fate tracking and how to reach the Trialmaster.
description: A reference for the Trial of Chaos in Path of Exile 2: modifier tiers, room objectives, build-specific hard stops, when to cash out, Fate sources and the path to the Trialmaster.
prerequisites: The Temple of Chaos unlocked (Act 3 Trial of Chaos cleared)
A character that survives Chaos trial Afflictions
Some Relics collected to stabilise deeper floors
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: The Trialmaster, the hidden boss of the Trial of Chaos in Path of Exile 2

items.title: What is the Trial of Chaos loop?
body: The Trial of Chaos runs in a repeating loop of rooms. Each cycle presents three Tribulations (modifiers); you pick one, clear the room, and the choice stacks with previous ones.
The loop continues until you choose to stop, cash out rewards, or fail.

items.title: Quest Ultimatum vs Inscribed Ultimatum?
body: The first Quest Ultimatum is the story gate. After that you use Inscribed Ultimatums (and higher-tier versions) to enter repeatable trials for Fate and rewards.

items.title: Why did I finish but get no Ascendancy points?
body: The Trial of Chaos grants points only through its boss rooms and the Trialmaster route. Simply surviving rooms banks rewards and Fate, not points; points come from the boss checkpoints and the Trialmaster.

items.title: What are the three Fates for?
body: Fate currencies are spent to open the door to the Trialmaster, the hidden boss that drops unique rewards and completes the Chaos Ascendancy ladder.

sections.title: Access and token types
paragraphs: Entry uses an Ultimatum item. The Quest Ultimatum is consumed once during the campaign; afterwards Inscribed Ultimatums and their upgraded tiers are the repeatable keys.
Higher-tier Ultimatums start at a deeper floor and present tougher modifier stacks, but also bank more reward value per run.
Keep a stock of appropriate-tier Ultimatums: low tiers for safe Fate farming, high tiers when your board can survive the stack.
bullets: Upgraded tiers = deeper start, bigger rewards

steps.label: Enter with an Ultimatum
body: Choose the tier that matches your current defensive board.

steps.label: Pick one of three Tribulations
body: Each room offers three modifiers; your pick is added to the running stack for the rest of the run.

steps.label: Clear the room objective
body: Survival, Defeat All, Escort, Soul Core or a boss antechamber, depending on the room.

steps.label: Decide: continue, cash out, or abort
body: Banked rewards and Fate are kept only if you cash out or survive to a checkpoint; failing loses the run's unbanked progress.

sections.title: Boss-room checkpoints
paragraphs: Boss rooms are the only rooms that advance the Ascendancy ladder inside the Trial of Chaos. Treat them as the real milestone, not the side rooms.
Before a boss room, top up Honour and confirm your damage can clear the boss phase. A stalled boss fight multiplies Honour pressure from the modifier stack.
If the stack is already dangerous, cash out before the boss room rather than gambling the ladder and losing the banked run.

sections.title: Reaching the Trialmaster
paragraphs: Once you hold the required Fate currencies, the door to the Trialmaster opens. The Trialmaster is the hidden boss of the Trial of Chaos and the source of its unique rewards.
The Trialmaster fight uses its own mechanics; this guide covers the path and preparation, while the boss page covers its attacks in detail.
Only attempt the Trialmaster once your board survives deep modifier stacks, since the encounter assumes a stabilised run.

sections.title: What players report
sections.intro: Community experiences; treat as strategy, not guaranteed math.

cards.title: Avoid stacking two damage modifiers
body: Players consistently report that two stacked damage modifiers are the most common brick, especially for squishy builds.

cards.title: Cash out beats greed
body: Many lost runs were one room past a safe cash-out; banking early is the norm among veteran runners.

cards.title: Fate is the real goal
body: The unique rewards behind the Trialmaster are why most farm the loop, not the per-room currency.

sections.title: Common problems
paragraphs: If you keep failing at the same modifier stack, stop picking damage modifiers and prioritise defence or escape-friendly rooms.
If you finished rooms but have no points, you likely skipped the boss checkpoint; points only advance at boss rooms and the Trialmaster.
If Fate is not accruing, confirm you are cashing out at checkpoints; unbanked progress is lost on failure.
